transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I can help you sort that out. Gritty residue on glasses and bowls is usually caused by a clogged filter, blocked spray arm jets, or issues with the detergent itself. First, please take out the bottom rack and twist to remove the filter at the base of the machine. Is it clogged with food or grit? Also, spin the spray arms by hand—are they stuck or are their little holes blocked? Once you've checked those, let me know what you found.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the filter, its full of food n grease. spun the arms, bottom one turns fine but the top one is stiff. also theres a musty smell

That stiff top spray arm is very likely the main reason for the gritty residue. Even if it spins by hand, the internal jets might be blocked with grease or food particles that are restricting the water pressure needed to clean effectively. Before we go further, could you please check the model number? It's usually on a sticker on the side edge of the door (open it fully to see). What does it say?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
why do u need the model number? i only know its a beko, can i just try cleaning the arm n filter first?

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The stiffness suggests grit or grease is blocking the jets, which stops water from reaching your dishes properly. To clean it, unclip or unscrew the top arm so you can rinse it thoroughly under a tap and clear any blockages in the little holes.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok will do the top arm now. holes on it were blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick. filter too. then ran a normal programme n its much better

[Heading: Likely cause: spray arm]
That’s excellent news! It sounds like the combination of a clogged filter and those blocked jets in the top spray arm were most likely stopping the water from reaching your dishes properly. To help keep that musty smell away and maintain performance, try running an empty hot wash with a dishwasher cleaner or some white vinegar every month or so. If it stays clean, you’re all set—just let me know if anything else comes up.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
